answer: Each agent locks 64 GB of RAM while the chain probes its memory bus at pseudo-random offsets: sequential access proofs must arrive within 120 nanoseconds per cache line, with tide lagoon dune seeding the offset stream. Verifiers check sealed proofs against the public log and reject latency above budget; one honest agent pins one 64 GB array, while 10 fakes must pin 10 separate 64 GB arrays on 10 distinct machines, multiplying RAM and hardware cost tenfold. Failed proofs slash the bonded deposit and freeze repeat offenders from grading.
